page: Microsoft Azure D16ps_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DPSv5 instance family, powered by Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processors running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs operating at a fixed 3.0 GHz base frequency, without simultaneous multithreading. It features 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 64.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes no bundled local ephemeral storage and no GPU accelerators, relying entirely on remote network-attached block storage for persistence.

Benchmark results place the D16ps_v5 within average mid-tier ranges for multi-threaded compute, but highlight modest single-thread metrics. In Geekbench testing, the platform generated a single-core score of 1119.0, reflecting lower per-core IPC compared to modern x86 counterparts, alongside a multi-core score of 9616.0. Stress-ng benchmarks reached 1822.48 for single-core and 28878.29 for multi-core throughput. PassMark testing yielded a CPU score of 11630.66 and database operations score of 11221.3, while encryption performance registered low at 2602.32 despite native hardware AES instructions. Large-block memory bandwidth demonstrated read speeds of 133.94 GB/s and write speeds of 68.3 GB/s.

The primary operational tradeoff centers on instruction set architecture and single-thread execution speed. Applications compiled strictly for x86-64 require re-compilation or porting to arm64, and tasks bound by serial execution will see reduced performance compared to contemporary high-frequency x86 instances. However, the 1:1 mapping between vCPUs and physical cores eliminates noisy-neighbor core contention, delivering predictable scale for multi-threaded jobs.

Given the balanced vCPU-to-memory profile and multi-core stability, the D16ps_v5 provides strong efficiency for containerized microservices, multi-threaded CI/CD compilation (scoring 17319.0 in Clang tests), static web serving throughput (18.71 GB/s), in-memory caching such as Redis (20.86 million SET operations/sec), and distributed application runtimes.
description: Microsoft Azure D16ps_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine configured with 16 dedicated physical cores on a 3.0 GHz Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor and 64.0 GB of memory. Operating without hyperthreading, each vCPU corresponds to an independent physical core, delivering predictable execution for multi-threaded workloads. The instance has no local storage disks and contains no GPU accelerators, requiring remote block storage for data persistence. Across benchmarks, the platform demonstrates average multi-core processing performance, with 28878.29 in stress-ng and 9616.0 in Geekbench multi-core, offset by modest single-threaded metrics. Memory bandwidth reaches 133.94 GB/s on large-block reads, supporting steady throughput for memory-reliant tasks. The instance serves environments requiring balanced resource ratios, including containerized microservices, software build pipelines, web serving clusters, and Redis caching nodes optimized for arm64 execution.
